forward_patch:
--- original
+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,26 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01KZFHBM7MWFYAMK3SQADF0D7H
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: ffa880
+title: 'duplication goes objective: sah duplicates tool rule supersedes the prompt rule'
+---
+Correction to ^3b49ewn. That card asked the wrong question. It compared detectors (jscpd against the in-house probe) and concluded the existing implementation stays — which kept duplication on the slowest component, an LLM pass. The point is review speed. The detector was never the problem: the in-house probe finds 3.5x the sites jscpd finds. The problem is that its output feeds a prompt rule. Make the detector the decider.
+
+Build:
+
+1. New sah op: run the `duplicates` detection (with the intra-file fix from ^adf0d7h) over the file arguments and emit one finding per line: `path:line: near-verbatim duplicate of <path:line> (similarity 0.97, <n> lines)`. Gate at similarity >= 0.95 — the near-verbatim class the prompt rule was told to flag. Below the gate is not a finding; no judgment tier remains.
+
+2. Structural test exclusion, deterministic: drop a finding whose span sits inside a test node — `#[cfg(test)]` / `#[test]` attributes in Rust, test-framework call/decorator/naming markers at the DEFINITION in the other grammars — decided by the tree-sitter parse, never by file path. This honors the no-path-based-test-exclusion rule with a machine fact instead of prose judgment.
+
+3. Inline suppression: an explicit marker comment on the block (pick one form, e.g. `// sah:allow duplication <reason>`, honored by the op across comment syntaxes). The exemption is in the code, never in prose.
+
+4. Tool rule `duplication-parsed` in the `duplication` set: files scope, `run: sah <op> "$@"`, `supersedes: [duplication, rust, swift]` — the whole set's prompt rules. Match lists the grammar roster's extensions; languages without a grammar keep the prompt path. Doctor names the sah binary; no install commands.
+
+5. Fixtures: fail = two near-verbatim 15-line blocks in one file (the intra-file case proves ^adf0d7h too); pass = the same shape below the gate, a suppressed copy with the marker, and a duplicate pair inside a `#[cfg(test)]` module. Extend the shipped-rules acceptance test. Acceptance: a review whose only defect is a pasted block reports it with zero LLM calls for the duplication set.
+
+Depends on ^adf0d7h.
+
+#tool-validators #objectivity #dead-code
\ No newline at end of file
